newsitem.title: RUSSIA: GUM estimates '96 GAAP net profit 137 bln rbls.
newsitem.headline: GUM estimates '96 GAAP net profit 137 bln rbls.

text.p: Russian retailer GUM said on Thursday 1996 net profit, calculated analogously to GAAP standards, was 137.3 billion roubles ($23.9 million) and that shareholders had approved a 1,000 rouble dividend for ordinary shares at its April 25 annual meeting.

GUM, which operates a chain of stores in Russia including its flagship mall across from the Kremlin on Red Square, said sales, to Russian accounting standards, were 1.33 trillion roubles, after 900.3 billion in 1996.
Net profit by Russian standards was 200.7 billion roubles after 134.0 billion in 1995, it said in a statement.
GUM's 1995 dividend was also 1,000 roubles per share.

OAO Torgovy Dom GUM said shareholders had not considered new issues but approved a share exchange giving 10 shares with a face value of 1,000 roubles each for every current 10,000-rouble share, which would not change authorised capital.
Pretax profit to Russian standards was 277.0 billion roubles, but comparatives were not available.
It was not clear if 1997 or 1996 Russian accounts were calculated on an accruals or cash basis.
